Formerly a part of a [[Kul Tiran Exploratory Fleet]] that shipwrecked on an isle in the South Seas, Lapidis quickly set to constructing a tower with the help of some of the Kul Tiran workers and his own elementals of water. Allying with both the trolls of Zul'Hazu and the ogres of the Gordosh Heights, he began working against the Exploratory Fleet that had established the settlement of [[Caelan's Rest]] and cut off all contact with them. Lapidis was an extremely powerful hydromancer and was considered to be more skilled than even those from Boralus. As he hid most of his studies and his work, how he had achieved such power was unknown, with some believing that he had assistance from either a magical artifact or an outside force. Prior to the Third War he had been invited to give a lesson on his studies of hydromancy within Dalaran, though he refused. ==Quotes== ;Aggro :Who let you in this tower?! Do you know who you are messing with?! ;Death :You know... Nothing... Lord '''Astalor Sunsworn''' is the Lord-Regent of Quel'Thalas,<ref name="A Good Day" /> the patriarch of House Sunsworn, and a current member of the [[Regency Council]] of [[Alah'Thalas]]. One of the surviving nobles of Quel'Thalas, Lord Sunsworn is amongst those most opposed to [[Vereesa Windrunner]], having aspirations to ascend to the throne himself and establish his own dynasty to replace House Sunstrider as rulers of the Quel'dorei.

==Biography==
Unlike other nobles of Silvermoon, Lord Sunsworn had kept his coffers in the vaults of [[Ironforge]], allowing him to maintain his vast fortunes even after the fall of Quel'Thalas. He would host lavish feasts for his fellow lords and ladies, though despite his claims that he opened his doors to the less fortunate as well,<ref name="A Good Day" /> he would requisition supplies meant for the impoverished of Quel'Thalas for feasts meant for his own supporters.<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|8|A Feast for the Poor}}</ref>

=== Scars of the Past ===
Lord Sunsworn was the one who convinced the Regency Council to open up [[Sunstrider Court]], a grand coliseum that was built within Alah'Thlas, to mercenaries, champions, and wanderers from all corners of Azeroth, each hoping to prove their strength, earn gold, or fight for something greater.<ref>[[Patch 1.18.0#NEW ARENA — SUNSTRIDER COURT]]</ref>

===Nightmares of Ursol===
In search of salvation for the Quel'dorei's magical addiction, Lord Sunsworn sent his cousin [[Andanil Sunsworn|Andanil]] to [[Moonwhisper Coast]] with an expedition in search of [[draenethyst]].<ref>[[Andanil Sunsworn#Quotes]]</ref> However, the expedition force did not send word back in weeks, prompting him to send an adventurer in search of Andanil.<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|53|Sunsworn Expedition}}</ref>

===''[[A Good Day]]''===
Following a campaign by the [[Silver Covenant]] to retake [[Shalandis Isle]], Lord Sunsworn exposed Vereesa Windrunner's funding for her campaign as having come from diverted funds intended for their people in exile and taxes that were owed to the Council, undermining her attempt at reclaiming her position as Speaker. As the ground that had been taken could not be forfeited to the Scourge after the matter had been disclosed, he made a motion before the Regency Council to have him be named Lord-Regent of Quel'Thalas, ostensibly to provide a strong leader to the people of Quel'Thalas in the dark times to come. With the five votes required from his fellow council members, he was named Lord-Regent of Quel'Thalas.<ref name="A Good Day" /><ref>[https://discord.com/channels/466622455805378571/528228771594240030/1447325402925109309 Lhian from the Turtle WoW Community Discord] - "its what happens between the high elf into and future quel thalas patch"</ref>

==Quotes==
;Gossip
Vereesa's ineptitude in rallying Alliance forces to reclaim Quel'Thalas marks the last straw. I refuse to witness our proud race reduced to a puppet state of Stormwind. With our reliance on the Alliance military, we stand exposed to the threats of both the Scourge and the resurgent Amani tribe.

It is only a matter of time until others recognize my rightful claim to leadership. The Sunsworn dynasty shall ascend, and under my rule, we will endure for countless millennia. The era of vulnerability and subservience is over; the domination of the Quel'dorei shall be reestablished, unyielding against external threats.

==Speculation==
He may be related to [[Priestess Maelah Sunsworn]] and [[Ranger Rubinah Sunsworn]].

Deceased (lore){{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frame of Atiesh (quest)|Frame of Atiesh}} }} '''Archmage Angela Dosantos''' is a [[human]] [[quest giver]] located at [[Light's Hope Chapel]] in the [[Eastern Plaguelands]]. A member of the [[Brotherhood of the Light]], a subsection of the [[Argent Dawn]]'s ranks, she offers quests to adventurers to collect [[Core of Elements]] to then exchange them with her for an [[Insignia of the Dawn]]. Angela was originally a member of the Kirin Tor of Dalaran, where her duties were to watch over the magical barriers protecting [[Atiest, Greatstaff of the Guardian|Atiesh]], the legendary greatstaff of the last Guardian of Tirisfal, [[Medivh]]. When the demon lord [[Archimonde]] destroyed [[Dalaran]], the barriers were broken and Atiesh was shattered into pieces. Dosantos left the Kirin Tor and began a search for the greatstaff which continues today. She first joined the Argent Dawn in order to help prevent [[Kel'Thuzad]] from gaining control of Atiesh, and has since been enrolled in the Brotherhood of the Light in order to pursue this goal more aggressively. However, when brought the rebuilt [[Frame of Atiesh]], she is driven to her death by [[Atiesh (demon)|Sargeras' corruption]] in the staff's frame, with her passing confirmed by [[Anachronos]]. ==Quests== * {{questlong|Neutral|60|The Elemental Equation}} {{queststartfinish}} ** {{questlong|Neutral|60|Core of Elements (quest)|Core of Elements}} {{dailyfinish}} * {{Neutral}} [60] [[The Dread Citadel - Naxxramas]] {{Queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Leggings (quest)|Frostfire Leggings|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Robe (quest)|Frostfire Robe|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Circlet (quest)|Frostfire Circlet|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Gloves (quest)|Frostfire Gloves|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Sandals (quest)|Frostfire Sandals|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Belt (quest)|Frostfire Belt|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Bindings (quest)|Frostfire Bindings|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Frostfire Shoulderpads (quest)|Frostfire Shoulderpads|class=mage}} {{queststartfinish}} ==Quotes== ===Gossip about Atiesh=== It is said that [[Kel'Thuzad]] seeks the legendary Atiesh, greatstaff of the Guardian. Yes, the very staff once held by [[Medivh]]. {{gossip|What is Atiesh?}} Like Kel'Thuzad, I too was once a mage of the [[Kirin Tor]]. And like Kel'Thuzad, I seek the legendary Atiesh, greatstaff of the Guardian. Our fates are intertwined as such, . {{gossip|What Guardian? I don't understand any of this.}} Progeny of [[Aegwynn]], he that would be the last Guardian of Tirisfal... Medivh. {{gossip|Please continue.}} It is a story of legend and one that I do not have the time nor the inclination to retell. Just know that Medivh was the last of the Guardians. The greatstaff of Atiesh was a focal point of his power and a focal point of corruption. {{gossip|What corruption?}} The corruption of a fallen titan. The corruption of the Destroyer. After all, the staff was forged from the seed of hate. That is, of course, what has brought me here... {{gossip|Please continue.}} After the fall of Karazhan, the Kirin Tor dispatched an assembly of mages to search the tower and seize all items of import... for the purposes of "research." It was then that the fabled staff was discovered and brought back to Dalaran. {{gossip|Please continue.}} What followed were a series of tragic events, leading to the death of every Kirin Tor mage that came into contact with Atiesh. You see, it was an artifact with sentience. A sentience granted to it by Sargeras... {{gossip|What?}} After the deaths, the Six decided that the best course of action was to seal the staff behind impenetrable barriers of magic and appoint a watcher: A guardian of the staff... I would be that watcher. {{gossip|This is disturbing. Please continue.}} There is not much more to tell. Dalaran was nearly wholly destroyed by Archimonde, the staff lost, presumably shattered by the barrier's fail-safe mechanisms. The '''arcane''' (also called the "'''arcane arts'''"<ref>[[Glyphic Memorandum]]</ref>) is a classification of magic. It is described as the base fabric of the world<ref>[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?quest=1880 Mage-tastic Gizmonitor]</ref>. The arcane is corruptive and addictive, and its use can draw the attention of the inhabitants of the Twisting Nether.

The arcane appears to be a general term that encompasses the magics used not only by mages, but by warlocks as well.

== Characteristics and use ==
The uses of the arcane are many, from creating blasts of raw power to conjuring food and water. Arcane can be called forth as the forces of frost and fire; according to Medivh, creating fire with the arcane is a matter of concentrating the inherent nature of fire in a location and calling it into being.<ref>''The Last Guardian'', pg. 24</ref> Incantations and hand movements are commonly used to invoke spells of the arcane, as are soul shards when summoning demons and other spellcasting. The arcane can be used to bind elementals into servitude,<ref>[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=2359 Elemental Slave]</ref> and construct magical golems.<ref>[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=60810 Arcane Golem]</ref>

Raw arcane magic materializes as a purplish colour.

== History ==
The Kaldorei Empire's ruling caste, a group of powerful spellcasters called the Highborne, delved deeply into the arcane. Under the guidance of Queen Azshara, they sought ways to access other dimensions. After Azshara's attempt to summon the demon-lord Kil'jaeden was thwarted and her empire toppled, the surviving night elves outlawed all practice of the arcane.

'''Archduke Keirich''' (High German pronunciation: ''ˈʃtɛlʊs ˈkaɪʁɪç''), born '''Stellus Keirich''', is a female [[Blood Death Knight]] affiliated with the [[Scourge]]. She is a noble scion of the fallen [[Kingdom of Lordaeron]] with maternal blood ties to [[Kul Tiras]]. In the *Chronicle of Myers*, she embodies the tragic elegance of Lordaeron's lost nobility blended with the untamed spirit of the sea, while wielding both runeblade and necrotic song.

== Biography ==

=== Early Life and Resurrection ===
Stellus Keirich was born in the capital of Lordaeron shortly before the outbreak of the Third War. Her father, Archmage Albert Keirich, was a highborn Lordaeronian noble of ancient Austrian-influenced lineage. Her mother was a woman from Kul Tiras — a seafaring nation known for its deep connection to the Tidemother and the waves. This mixed heritage gave young Stellus a unique blend of continental refinement and maritime resilience.

Condemned to death at birth for reasons shrouded in family secrecy, the infant was saved by her father through a forbidden ritual that combined Lordaeronian necromantic arts with enchanted music. This resurrection not only restored life but transformed Stellus's body from male to female, marking her as one of the most unusual rebirths in the eastern kingdoms. The ritual left a permanent echo of song within her soul — a gift and curse that would define her existence.

=== The Fall of Lordaeron and Path to Undeath ===
As the Scourge ravaged Lordaeron, Stellus witnessed the kingdom she loved crumble under Prince Arthas's betrayal. Already touched by death once, she was claimed by the Lich King's forces and raised as a [[Death Knight|Blood Death Knight]]. Unlike many who lost themselves to the plague, she retained fragments of her noble identity and her mother's seafaring spirit.

Even in service to the Scourge, Archduke Keirich maintains a degree of independence. She often wanders the plague-ridden lands of Tirisfal and the Western Plaguelands, where echoes of old Lordaeron still linger, occasionally venturing toward the coasts that remind her of her Kul Tiran blood.

=== The Musician of the Damned ===
Death could not silence the music that once saved her. Stellus channels necrotic energies through haunting melodies and guitar-like stringed instruments, creating songs that can soothe the restless dead, torment the living, or briefly awaken faint memories in other undead. She is fluent in both the Common tongue of Lordaeron (with a refined High German nobility accent) and the [[Kul Tiran (language)|Kul Tiran language]] inherited from her mother — a lyrical, wave-like dialect rich in nautical metaphors and rhythmic cadence (often compared by scholars to the flowing poetry of distant eastern isles).

She co-founded the shadowy musical ensemble HOSIBOSI with her wife Hoshino Ryoko and serves as mentor to Shibatou Atsumi, guiding them through both the shadows of undeath and the remnants of mortal artistry.

== Appearance ==
Archduke Keirich stands approximately 170 cm tall with a graceful yet battle-hardened physique. She has vibrant orange-red hair usually tied in a high right-side ponytail, and glowing ice-blue eyes that betray her Death Knight nature. Her skin is eerily pale and smooth, retaining an almost lifelike quality due to her unique resurrection. She alternates between heavy rune-etched plate armor bearing Lordaeronian crests and flowing garments reminiscent of Kul Tiran seafarer fashion.

== Personality ==
Keirich is charismatic, resilient, and pragmatic. She carries the refined pride of Lordaeron nobility tempered by the free-spirited resilience of Kul Tiras. The traumas of her birth, transformation, and kingdom's fall have forged a strong will and a quiet melancholy. She is fiercely protective of her family and protégés, yet maintains a detached amusement toward the endless conflicts of the living and the dead.

== Abilities ==
As a Blood Death Knight, her powers focus on blood magic and self-sustainment:
* '''Blood Boil''': Spreads disease and pain through corrupted blood.
* '''Death Strike''': Delivers shadow-infused blows that heal her wounds.
* '''Rune Tap''': Strengthens her defenses with runic power.

Her mother's Kul Tiran heritage grants her the ability to infuse songs with necrotic magic, allowing performances to influence emotions, drain life force, or offer rare moments of solace to the undead.

== Relationships ==
* '''Albert Keirich (Father)''': The Lordaeronian archmage who performed her resurrection and shaped her early power.
* '''Hoshino Ryoko (Wife)''': Her steadfast companion in both life and undeath, sharing musical and personal bonds.
* '''Hoshino Atsuko / Hoshino Kadosada (Child)''': The next generation of her unconventional family.
* '''Shibatou Atsumi (Protégé)''': A young talent she guides and protects.

== Trivia ==
* She speaks with a refined High German (Austrian-style) accent in Common, a remnant of her Lordaeronian noble upbringing.
* She is fluent in the Kul Tiran language, often using its rhythmic, sea-inspired phrases in songs or private moments.
* Her mixed Lordaeron-Kul Tiras heritage makes her a bridge between continental nobility and maritime culture, even after becoming undead.

'''Archimonde''' was one of the most "faithful" subjects of the fallen [[titan]], [[Sargeras]]. Archimonde is one of the [[Eredar]] [[demon]]s, who forged the first of the [[warlock]] magics. His ruthless and cunning personality quickly earned him station and power within the Eredar ranks, until finally he was first among them.

Arguably the second most powerful creature, second to [[Kil'jaeden]], ever to set hoof in the world of Azeroth (besides the titans or the old gods).

When [[Azshara]]'s reckless magics began to attract the attention of Sargeras, Archimonde and [[Mannoroth]] led the catastrophic, destructive invasion. With thousands of demonic servants in their wake, they poured through the portal beneath the [[Well of Eternity]], and were let loose upon the ancient land of [[Kalimdor]], razing and bloodletting every structure and creature they came across.

However, a young scholar, [[Malfurion Stormrage]], gathered a small band of [[night elves]], and, with the help of [[Cenarius]]' woodland allies and [[Alexstrasza]]'s mighty dragon flights, they managed to beat back the demonic hordes, and, in a titanic battle, the portal became unstable and collapsed, sundering the world, and banishing Archimonde and his minions back into the burning pits of the [[Twisting Nether]].

Archimonde brooded for ten thousand years in the dark recesses of the Twisting Nether as they planned for a new invasion. His colleague, Kil'jaeden, found the means through [[Ner'zhul]] and, eventually, [[Gul'dan]], on the dying, ancient world of [[Draenor]]. With Mannoroth's sinister help, the chieftains of the [[orc]]ish Hordes were corrupted, and a bloodlust came over them that swept them into a tumultuous frenzy that engulfed their world. The orcs were to be the harbinger of the [[Legion]]'s return, destroying all they beheld so that none could oppose the Legion. However, after the exodus into Azeroth and Draenor's eventual destruction, the Horde was defeated by the [[human]]s of former [[Arathor]], and they failed in their unholy mission.

However, an old tool was found that could once again be put to use. Ner'zhul, the dark [[shaman]] of the [[Shadowmoon Clan]], was sent spiraling with his most faithful disciples into the Twisting Nether after attempting to find new worlds to control, and he was found by Kil'jaeden and the Burning Legion. Over time, he was transformed into the [[Lich King]], an ethereal spirit that controlled the [[undead]] [[Scourge]], a force so mighty, that it was expected to succeed where the Horde had failed. They did.

Archimonde was chosen to lead the second coming of the Legion, but he needed the means of getting to Azeroth. A being with as much tremendous power as an Eredar needed more magic to summon than a simple [[Nathrezim]], and he waited until finally he was contacted by [[Kel'Thuzad]] the Summoner, who, after stealing the [[Book of Medivh]] from [[Dalaran]], began the lengthy summoning process. As he proceeded, the skies were split asunder, and mighty [[infernal]]s and [[felhound]]s were brought to aid the Scourge. Finally, it was completed, and Archimonde was brought into the world of Azeroth.

Archimonde first placed [[Tichondrius]] in charge of the Scourge, saying that there was no longer any need of the Lich King.

Then, Archimonde proceeded to single-handedly destroy the city of Dalaran using an ancient Eredar spell.

The invasion of [[Lordaeron]] continued unabated, the magics of Archimonde and Tichondrius summoning hordes of demonic followers, including the diabolical [[Pit Lord]], Mannoroth. Together, they plowed through the nations of Lordaeron, devastating all they beheld. However, Tichondrius soon found that the orcs were missing. The Legion followed them across the sea, where they found not only the orcs but also, the vile night elves who had banished them millennia before. He even met [[Tyrande]], the insolent leader of the [[Sentinels]], who woke the ancient druids, and together, they battled the Legion once again.

Archimonde became aware, then, of a substantial power that hadn't been there before. It was [[Alexstrasza]]'s [[World Tree]], [[Nordrassil]]. It kept the night elves immortal, and granted them their powers over nature. Finally, Archimonde threw the plans of Kil'jaeden and the Legion to the wind. He knew that if he could harness the World Tree's powers for himself, he would be as powerful as Sargeras himself. But, there was resistance in the way. Tyrande and Malfurion had allied with [[Thrall]] and [[Jaina Proudmoore]], and Archimonde was forced to slowly ascended [[Mount Hyjal]], destroying every successive base with the help of [[Azgalor]], a Pit Lord, [[Rage Winterchill]], a lich, and [[Anetheron]], his most loyal Nathrezim.  Archimonde's Buildings were better versions of the [[Undead]] buildings.


With his ascension going very well, Archimonde didn't notice the ancestral spirits that were amassing at the base of the World Tree.  And as he slaughtered the mortals and their bases, he went heedlessly to the Tree, and began to climb it to claim his power, completely unaware of the trap that Malfurion had set for him. All he knew was that as he neared the Tree, he was growing in size and power, and he was resolved that nothing would stop him.


As Archimonde climbed, Malfurion raised the [[Horn of Cenarius]] and called to the ancestral guardians. They rose from the forest and amassed around Archimonde. They fell upon him, detonating in a massive explosion that destroyed the demon warlock and incinerated the forests around the World Tree; nature herself would not allow his defilement to occur.

Archimonde's brief presence in the world left a terrible scar, though, and it is a fearful idea that he was not the leader, merely the subordinate, of his unholy order.

{{NPC||Torlath Ironhard|icon=Human Male}} | tabard = ArgentTabard.png }} The '''Argent Dawn''' (referred to as simply the '''Dawn''')[[Gregor Greystone#Quotes]] is an organization focused on protecting [[Azeroth]] from agencies that seek to destroy it, such as the [[Burning Legion]] and the [[Scourge]]. As a worldwide organization maintaining a status of neutrality, the Argent Dawn is not a political body, nor do their members ever wish to become one. Their cause is to fight swiftly and mercilessly against any element of evil that surfaced in Azeroth. To that end, they call both the [[Alliance]] and the [[Horde]] allies in the cause of stamping out evil and therefore recruit from all races without distinction.[[Argent Officer Pureheart#Quotes]] Their base camps can be found across all the [[Plaguelands]] as well as in [[Tirisfal Glades]], while their agents are also present in [[Stormwind City]], [[Darnassus]], and [[Everlook]]. ==Background== :'''''S'''ome say that it is always darkest just before the dawn. Whenever darkness falls, the light of hope will drive away the shadows; wherever the forces of evil work in secret, the brave men and women of the Argent Dawn will be there to thwart their dark designs. The Argent Dawn is an organization that makes no distinction between Alliance or Horde, but instead tries to unite the people of Azeroth in the fight against evil. Though the agents of the Argent Dawn are always wary of the sinister and the wicked in all their various disguises, they have recently focused their efforts on a region of Azeroth where evil has run unchecked for a long time: the Plaguelands of Lordaeron. Detachments of the Argent Dawn are guarding the entrances to the Plaguelands at the Bulwark between the Tirisfal Glades and the western Plaguelands, and at Chillwind Point, a narrow pass leading south from the eastern Plaguelands to the Alterac Mountains. They have also gained a foothold deep in the eastern Plaguelands at the Light's Hope Chapel, east of Corin’s Crossing.'' :''The Argent Dawn is always looking for more fighters to join their cause, and the numbers of those wearing the Argent Dawn Commission, the organization’s insignia, are growing each day. Adventurers seeking to aid the Argent Dawn by rooting out the Scourge’s corruption in the Plaguelands and taking on the Lich King’s powerful servants in the Scholomance and Stratholme will be well rewarded; the organization has many powerful enchanters among their ranks who craft special enhancements that provide the wearer with added protection against all forms of magical attacks. The Argent Dawn also offers those who have proven their dedication to their cause insight into their craftsmen’s designs, enabling these adventurers to craft the armors the Argent Dawn created in their ongoing campaign against evil.''[https://web.archive.org/web/20060218080014/http://www.wow-europe.com/en/info/basics/factions/argent/index.html World of Warcraft - Classic Factions - Argent Dawn] (Retrieved 21st Feb 2006) ==History== ===Founding=== The Argent Dawn was originally formed as a splinter faction of the [[Scarlet Crusade]]. The Scarlet Crusade was formed by Highlord [[Alexandros Mograine]], [[High General Abbendis]] and [[Grand Inquisitor Isillien]] during the [[Third War]]. Under Mograine's leadership, the Scarlet Crusade was at first a noble order, and Mograine was dubbed the Ashbringer as it would be all that remained of the undead after he would walk into whole battalions of undead and emerge unscathed. However, Mograine proved to be the lynchpin of the Crusade, and when joined by [[Saidan Dathrohan]] - who was in fact impersonated by the dreadlord [[Balnazzar]] - corruption began to spread throughout the Crusade, planting the seeds of madness and insane zealotry that the order became infamous for.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Corrupted_Ashbringer/Scarlet_Monastery_Event Corrupted Ashbringer/Scarlet Monastery Event] Becoming Grand Crusader of the Scarlet Crusade, Dathrohan made a bargain with [[Kel'Thuzad]] and arranged for Alexandros to be ambushed during a foray in [[Stratholme]]. While the undead attack was not enough, it exhausted him enough that his son [[Renault Mograine|Renault]] was able to claim the Ashbringer and drive it through his father's heart while his back was turned. The heinous act of betrayal corrupted the blade and led to Mograine's own corruption as a death knight of the Scourge and champion of Kel'Thuzad. [[High Inquisitor Fairbanks]], who had bore witness to the Highlord's death, returned to the [[Scarlet Monastery]] - much to Renault's dismay. Shouting and screaming, he told the tale of the lesser Mograine's betrayal to any and all who would hear him. While Fairbanks was murdered in cold blood for his actions and dragged to a hidden chamber of the Monastery Cathedral, some did listen to his words, and thus they separated from the Crusade to form the Argent Dawn. ===World of Warcraft=== [[File:Light's Hope Chapel.png|thumb|300px|[[Light's Hope Chapel]] in the [[Eastern Plaguelands]], the headquarters of the Argent Dawn.]] In time, the Argent Dawn settled [[Argent Dawn embassy|an embassy]] in [[Darnassus]] and [[The Argent Dawn (Stormwind)|another one]] in [[Stormwind City]]. In [[Lordaeron]], [[Argent Officer Pureheart]] at [[Chillwind Camp]], and [[Argent Officer Garush]] at the [[Bulwark]], recruited various [[adventurer]]s to slay the undead. They gave them [[Argent Dawn Commission|commision trinkets]],{{questlong|Both|55|Argent Dawn Commission (quest)|Argent Dawn Commission}} and the heroes in turn delivered them the [[scourgestone]]s of the Scourge from across the [[Plaguelands]].{{questlong|Neutral|55|Minion's Scourgestones}}{{questlong|Neutral|55|Invader's Scourgestones}}{{questlong|Neutral|55|Corruptor's Scourgestones}} They also sent their subordinate, [[Gregor Greystone]], to [[Everlook]] in [[Winterspring]] to represent the Argent Dawn's interests to the local governance of the [[Steamwheedle Cartel]].{{questlong|Both|52|The Everlook Report}} The organization was also investigating [[Twilight Lord Kelris]], but he eluded them, and sometimes they thought him dead or missing. They also knew that whenever evil made its presence known in Kalimdor, Kelris had played a role.{{questlong|Both|27D|Blackfathom Villainy}} When many rumors circulate about the union of the [[Twilight's Hammer]] and the [[naga]] on the coasts of [[Ashenvale]], the Dawn sent [[Argent Guard Thaelrid]] to check on the activity in [[Blackfathom Deeps]]. However, he was grievously wounded after he found out that the cultists, led by Kelris, sacrificed innocents to the [[hydra]] [[Aku'mai]] for power.{{questlong|Alliance|24D|In Search of Thaelrid}} In [[Desolace]], [[Azore Aldamort]] engages the services of adventurers to retrieve the [[Sceptre of Light]] held by the minions of the [[Burning Blade]] within the [[Thunder Axe Fortress]].{{questlong|Neutral|33|Sceptre of Light (quest)|Sceptre of Light}} He is also determined to unravel the secrets of [[naga]] and sends them to acquire the [[Book of the Ancients]] on [[Ranazjar Isle]].{{questlong|Neutral|38|Book of the Ancients (quest)|Book of the Ancients}} [[File:Argent Dawn camp Stormwind.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A camp of the Argent Dawn settled within [[Stormwind City]] during the [[Scourge Invasion]].]] During the [[Scourge Invasion]], several regions of [[Azeroth]] came under attack by Scourge forces. Subsequently, the Argent Dawn organized a worldwide counter to the undead invasion, keeping an eye out for any [[necropolis]] sightings and passing on their information to all adventurers willing to aid them in their struggle. As more and more invasion attempts were beaten back by the defenders, the Argent Dawn was able to bestow increasingly more powerful blessings upon those fighting the invaders. Those who wished to take up arms against the undead invaders could speak with a representative of the organization to learn what regions needed help and how the defense was holding up. When necropolises appeared outside the [[Alliance]] and [[Horde]] capitals, the Argent Dawn heeded their desperate call for help, setting up camps inside the besieged cities and rallying the defense against the undead.[http://web.archive.org/web/20060826233658/http://www.worldofwarcraft.com:80/info/events/scourgeinvasion/ Archived page] Regardless of their influence, the Argent Dawn did not have the manpower of the [[Scarlet Crusade]], and could not stand alone against the [[Scourge]]. A sub-faction of the Dawn, named the [[Brotherhood of the Light]] under the lead of [[Commander Eligor Dawnbringer]], worked to keep relations between both organizations from growing violent.{{questlong|Neutral|60R|Echoes of War}} As such, they formed an uneasy alliance in order to focus their combined strength against [[Kel'Thuzad]]'s forces in the [[Plaguelands]]. When they learned that the [[necromancer]]s of the [[Cult of the Damned]] were creating their own [[plagued dragon]]s in [[Scholomance]], they worked to destroy the creatures before they could be deployed.{{questlong|Neutral|58D|Plagued Hatchlings (quest)|Plagued Hatchlings}} Despite their tenuous alliance, [[Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff]] condemns the Scarlet Crusade as blasphemers and directs adventurers to slay [[Archivist Galford]] and burn down his archives, in order to take away their most valued documents and punish them for their heretical zealotry.{{questlong|Neutral|60D|The Archivist}} When the heroes confronted [[Grand Crusader Dathrohan]], they discovered that was being impersonated by the [[nathrezim]] [[Balnazzar]], and brought back his [[Head of Balnazzar|head]] as proof of the demon's masquerade. This discovery shocked Zverenhoff who pondered what the ramifications of Balnazzar's corruption would have on the zealots should the truth come out.{{questlong|Neutral|60D|The Truth Comes Crashing Down}} Duke Zverenhoff later ordered the heroes to slay [[Baron Rivendare]],{{questlong|Neutral|60D|Above and Beyond}} and those who accomplished such a task were rewarded by [[Lord Maxwell Tyrosus]] himself with an access to the [[Argent Hold]].{{questlong|Neutral|60|The Argent Hold}} ==Reputation== Reputation with the Argent Dawn can be gained in four ways. ===Killing Scourge=== The primary method of gaining favor is to kill undead Scourge across the Plaguelands, [[Scholomance]], [[Stratholme]] and [[Naxxramas]]. Non-elite mobs will stop giving reputation once halfway through friendly, save for [[Shadowmage]]s that continue even though honored. Elite mobs stop giving reputation once halfway through honored. It is recommended to max out reputation via killing before progressing on to Scourgestone quests. ===Scourgestones=== At level 50, players will be able to receive missions from the Argent Dawn. [[Argent Officer Pureheart]] at [[Chillwind Camp]] and [[Argent Officer Garush]] at the [[Bulwark]] can give out an [[Argent Dawn Commission]] trinket that allows players to loot [[Scourgestone]]s when killing agents of the Scourge throughout the [[Western Plaguelands|Western]] and [[Eastern Plaguelands]] while equipped. Scourgestones can be turned in at the Bulwark, Chillwind Camp, or Light's Hope Chapel to raise your reputation with the Dawn. The quest {{questlong|Neutral|60D|The Active Agent}} rewards the player with either [[Seal of the Dawn]] or [[Rune of the Dawn]], each acting as alternative trinkets to the Argent Dawn Commendation while granting extra bonuses against the undead. [[Mark of the Champion]], from {{questlong|Neutral|60R|The Fall of Kel'Thuzad}}, is another powerful alternative. There are three types of Scourgestones, each requiring a different amount to be able to be turned in for reputation and an [[Argent Dawn Valor Token]], which can be used either to further increase your reputation or used as currency to buy special items at higher reputation levels. * [[Minion's Scourgestone]] - Collect 20 * [[Invader's Scourgestone]] - Collect 10 * [[Corruptor's Scourgestone]] - Collect 1 ===Cauldron Quests=== Upon completion of the Plague Cauldrons questline, you will be able to obtain a [[Vitreous Focuser]] from either {{NPC|Alliance|Alchemist Arbington|}} in [[Chillwind Camp]] or {{NPC|Horde|Apothecary Dithers|}} at the [[Bulwark]], which will allow you to collect Osseous Agitators, Somatic Intensifiers, and Ectoplasmic Resonators. These, combined with runecloth and an [[Arcane Quickener]] purchased from the same NPC, will allow you to change the composition of the plague that the cauldrons create into something that negatively affects the Scourge, which will earn you additional reputation with the Argent Dawn. The four cauldrons are located at: * [[Felstone Field]] * [[Dalson's Tears]] * [[Writhing Haunt]] * [[Gahrron's Withering]] ===Healthy Dragon Scales=== Once you have completed the entire Egg-Freezing quest line (which starts with [http://www.thottbot.com/?n=7956 Tinkee Steamboil] in the Burning Steppes and eventually takes you to [http://www.thottbot.com/?n=4715 Betina Bigglezink] in the Eastern Plaguelands), you will be able to receive [http://www.thottbot.com/?i=21977 Healthy Dragon Scales] as drops from the Plagued Whelps in [[Scholomance]]. As only a few may drop per run and the favor received is equal to that of a Valor Token or turning in a load of Scourgestones, it is not a very productive way to farm reputation. ==Patch changes== * {{Patch|1.18.0|note=New reputation rewards can be bough from [[Torlath Ironhard]].}} * [[File:WoWlogo.png|40px]] '''Patch 1.7.0 (2005-09-13):''' Argent Dawn vendors now show you their entire inventory regardless of current reputation, allowing players to peruse their full range of wares. '''Arathor''' was the first great [[human nation]], founded by a unification of the various tribes of the [[Eastern Kingdoms]] under the [[Arathi]].  Its capital was [[Strom]], now known as the semi-abandoned fortress of [[Stromgarde]].

==Creation and the Troll Wars==
Concerned that the [[Troll War|troll]]s were becoming too great a threat, the Arathi tribe embarked on a campaign to conquer its rivals through combat and politics.  By offering equality and peace to the people they conquered, the Arathi were able to form a powerful nation, Arathor.  The capital of Strom was built, and the humans in the area that would become [[Lordaeron]] travelled to its protection.

The [[high elf|high elves]] of [[Quel'Thalas]], meanwhile, were also under threat of the trolls.  On the verge of defeat, they sent ambassadors to Strom to plead for assistance from the human king, [[Thoradin]].  In exchange for support, the elves agreed to instruct one hundred humans in the use of magic.  Through the military might of Stromgarde, and the magic wielded by the elves and new human [[Mage (lore)|mages]], the trolls were soundly defeated.

==Fracturing of the Kingdom==
Following the defeat of the trolls, the human mages that had been instructed by the elves eventually chose to leave Strom and found their own kingdom, [[Dalaran]], dedicated to the study and use of magic.  In time, other city-states were founded: [[Gilneas]], [[Alterac]], and [[Kul Tiras]].  Much of the nobility moved to the fertile lands of the north, founding [[Lordaeron]], while the heirs of King Thoradin travelled far south to form the kingdom of [[Azeroth]](later known as [[Stormwind]]).  The few remaining loyal defenders of Strom renamed it [[Stromgarde]], all that was left of a once-great empire.

==Modern Ramifications==
The human nations that splintered off from Arathor would not be united again until the [[Second War]], in which the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]] was formed to defeat the [[Old Horde|Horde]].  Lord [[Anduin Lothar]], as the last descendant of the Arathi, was able to call upon the [[high elf|high elves]] to join the Alliance, in payment of the help provided by the humans of Arathor during the troll wars.

The zone is also a major travel hub for both [[Horde]] and [[Alliance]], even at higher levels. ==Geography== Ashenvale is a forest full of ancient trees, teeming with life. '''Archmage Arugal''' is a former mage of Dalaran who lives within the ruins of Shadowfang Keep.

==General Information==
*Level: 26 [[Elite]]
*[[:Category:Zones|Location]]: [[Shadowfang Keep]]
*[[Creature type|Type]]: [[Creature type#Humanoid|Humanoid]]

==Background==
Arugal was once a member of the [[Kirin Tor]] of [[Dalaran]]. However after the [[Scourge]] destroyed Dalaran and many of the wizards died in battle and rose soon after, adding their former might to the growing Scourge, he fled to [[Shadowfang Keep]] which looms above [[Pyrewood Village]]. Frustrated by their lack of progress and against the advice of his peers Arugal elected to summon extra-dimensional entities to bolster Dalaran's diminishing ranks. Arugal's summoning brought the ravenous [[Worgen]] into the world of [[Azeroth]]. The feral wolf-men slaughtered not only the Scourge, but quickly turned on the wizards themselves. The worgen sieged the keep of the noble, [[Baron Silverlaine]]. Situated above the tiny hamlet of Pyrewood, the keep quickly fell into shadow and ruin. Driven mad with guilt, Arugal adopted the Worgen as his children and retreated to the newly dubbed 'Shadowfang Keep'. He still resides there, protected by his massive pet, [[Fenrus]] - and haunted by the vengeful ghost of Baron Silverlaine.

A group of adventurers loyal to the [[Dark Lady]] entered Shadowfang Keep to ascertain the whereabouts of two Deathstalkers and to slay the Archmage. As they entered the Keep the adventurers found Arugal taunting Deathstalker Vincent before having several worgen rip the Deathstalker apart. As Vincent was being mauled Arugal said "If you will not serve my Master with your sword and knowledge of his enemies...your smoldering remains will serve me as a testament to what happens when one is foolish enough to enter my domain." After the Deathstalker died Arugal retreated deep within the Keep but the group of adventurers fought their way through Argual’s minions and slew the Archmage. The identity of the “Master” that Arugal mentioned still remains unknown but some believe that this person is the same one who controls the Dark Riders that have been seen coming out of [[Deadwind Pass]] to harass the citizens of [[Duskwood]]. Others could reasonably speculate that this "Master" is in fact the [[Lich King]] whose minions were reported stalking the dark and dusty corridors of the Keep at the time of the [[Scourge Invasion]].

==Abilities==
*'''Shadowbolt''' Deals massive amount of [[shadow]] damage to single target.
*'''Teleport''' Teleports to random spot in the room, and then throws shadow bolts to your group.
*'''Worgen''' Turn your party member to Worgen, making it lose control and attack on you.

==Strategy==
Archmage Arugal is the toughest boss from the low level instances, and you may wipe on this. The best tactic is to pull him to the lower floor, and try to siphon his mana off, so he cannot teleport away. All ranged DPS should go to upper floor so they won't lose line of sight to Arugal, even if he teleports. Also, when a party member is turned to Worgen, remember that priests or paladins can dispel the transformation.

As the high elves fought for their lives against the trolls' fierce onslaught, the scattered, nomadic humans of Lordaeron fought to consolidate their own tribal lands. The tribes of early humanity raided each other's settlements with little heed for racial unification or honor. Yet one tribe, known as the Arathi, saw that the trolls were becoming too great a threat to ignore. The Arathi wished to bring all of the tribes under its rule so that they could provide a unified front against the troll warbands. Over the course of six years, the cunning Arathi outmaneuvered and outfought the rival tribes. After every victory, the Arathi offered peace and equality to the conquered people; thus, they won the loyalty of those they had beaten. Eventually the Arathi tribe came to include many disparate tribes, and the ranks of its army grew vast. Confident that they could hold their own against the troll warbands or even the reclusive elves if need be, the Arathi warlords decided to construct a mighty fortress city in the southern regions of Lordaeron. The city-state, named Strom, became the capital of the Arathi nation, Arathor. As Arathor prospered, humans from all over the vast continent traveled south to the protection and safety of Strom. United under one banner, the human tribes developed a strong, optimistic culture. Thoradin, the king of Arathor, knew that the mysterious elves in the northlands were under constant siege by the trolls, but refused to risk the safety of his people in defense of reclusive strangers. Many months passed as rumors of the elves' supposed defeat trickled down from the north. It was only when weary ambassadors from Quel'Thalas reached Strom that Thoradin realized how great the troll threat truly was. The elves informed Thoradin that the troll armies were vast and that once the trolls had destroyed Quel'Thalas, they would move on to attack the southlands. The desperate elves, in dire need of military aid, hastily agreed to teach certain select humans to wield magic in exchange for their help against the warbands. Thoradin, distrustful of any magic, agreed to aid the elves out of necessity. Almost immediately, elven sorcerers arrived in Arathor and began to instruct a group of humans in the ways of magic. The elves found that although humans were innately clumsy in their handling of magic, they possessed a startling natural affinity for it. One hundred men were taught the very basics of the elves' magical secrets: no more than was absolutely necessary to combat the trolls. Convinced that their human students were ready to aid in the struggle, the elves left Strom and traveled north alongside the mighty armies of King Thoradin. The united elf and human armies clashed against the overwhelming troll warbands at the foot of the Alterac Mountains. The battle lasted for many days, but the unflagging armies of Arathor never tired or gave an inch of ground before the troll onslaught. The elven lords deemed that the time had come to release the powers of their magic upon the enemy. The hundred human magi and a multitude of elven sorcerers called down the fury of the heavens and set the troll armies ablaze. The elemental fires prevented the trolls from regenerating their wounds and burned their tortured forms from the inside out. As the troll armies broke and attempted to flee, Thoradin's armies ran them down and slaughtered every last one of their soldiers. The trolls would never fully recover from their defeat, and history would never see the trolls rise as one nation again. Assured that Quel'Thalas was saved from destruction, the elves made a pledge of loyalty and friendship to the nation of Arathor and to the bloodline of its king, Thoradin. Humans and elves would nurture peaceful relations for ages to come.

== Background ==
Ashbringer, the Blade of the Scarlet Highlord, is an object of great mystery and power. 

Several characters have mentioned the Ashbringer on occasion, but the only beings believed to know the current location of the Ashbringer are [[Nat Pagle]], Master Fisherman, and [[Prince Tortheldrin]], the leader of the [[Shen'dralar]] within [[Dire Maul]]. Getting the full story from them has proven difficult, but Tortheldrin's followers claim that he may be willing to tell what he knows if a player were to defeat the dragon Nefarian and share the tale with him. Some have brought Nefarian's head to Tortheldrin, though he said nothing that lead to the Ashbringer.

The corrupted Ashbringer is currently held by [[Highlord Mograine]] and is a drop of [[The Four Horsemen]] in [[Naxxramas]]. The corrupted Ashbringer starts a quest in the Cathedral of the [[Scarlet Monastery]]. Once the wearer of the Ashbringer enters the Cathedral, an event starts with the following words:

"Scarlet Commander Mograine yells: Bow down! Kneel before the Ashbringer! A new dawn approaches, brothers and sisters! Our message will be delivered to the filth of the new world through the chosen one." 

[[High Inquisitor Fairbanks]] offers the continuation of the quest of the Ashbringer by telling its full story: How Mograine rose to become Highlord, founder of the Scarlet Crusade and known under the title Ashbringer, because of his might in slaying the undead. The sword was crafted for him and became attuned to him. He died through the betrayal of his son, [[Scarlet Commander Mograine]] to Kel'Thuzad. The scourge sent an army to defeat the Highlord, but the Highlord slew the scourge legion. After more legions were sent, Fairbanks fell in battle and woke only to see that "the lesser Mograine" had killed his father with the sword.

Because the sword is tied to his wielder and the tale, it has become corrupted when Mograine became a death knight. High Inquisitor Fairbanks states that it can only be restored by Mograine's second son, who stays in Outland.

It is believed that the restoration of the Ashbringer can only be done once the Expansion "The Burning Crusade" is out.

This item is not currently in game as posted on the World of Warcraft General forums, by the community manager Eyonix: "It's true that currently Ashbringer is not in the game, although one day in the future it will be, but not until after there is an awesome legendary item for casters. ;)"

'''Archmage Modera''' is a [[human]] mage and a member of the [[Council of Six]], the [[Kirin Tor]] high council of [[Dalaran (kingdom)|Dalaran]]. She appears to be one of the most long-standing members of the Six, having been active as a member during the [[Second War]] up until now.

==History==
===Aftermath of the Second War===
As a member of the council, Modera was present at the meetings of the secret council where the members discussed the possible return of [[Deathwing]] following the war. The council, [[Krasus]] especially, chose [[Rhonin]] to send him on a mission to investigate whether Deathwing had really returned. The ruling mages then learned about a mysterious person known as Daval Prestor who was rumored to be Deathwing. Modera and [[Drenden]] then worked to discover if it was true and thus traveled to the [[Capital City]] to meet both, [[Terenas Menethil II|Terenas]] and Prestor. They were unable to discover more about Prestor. Thanks to the efforts of Rhonin, Krasus, [[Vereesa Windrunner|Vereesa]] and many others, Deathwing was defeated once more and Modera was present at the final meeting where the members summarized what has happened.<ref>''[[Day of the Dragon]]''</ref>

Shortly before the [[Third War]], Modera spoke out against [[Kel'Thuzad]]'s use of necromancy. She was present when his experiments were discovered, accusing him that his methods would see them condemned as heretics, and leading to his expulsion from the [[Kirin Tor]].<ref>''[[Road to Damnation]]''</ref>

===Mysteries of Azeroth===
While Modera has survived the Third War and the destruction of Dalaran at the hands of [[Archimonde]], to this day she remains in Dalaran to oversee the rebuilding of the city. Her daughter [[Magistrate Modera|Caitlyn]] traveled to [[Northwind]] to represent Dalaran in the Northwind Joust.<ref>[[Magistrate Modera#Quotes]]</ref>
